title: Hydrogen iodide equilibrium from particle diagrams

stimulus.title: Two snapshots of one container
stimulus.html:
Key: H2I2HI

Hydrogen and iodine react in a sealed 1.0 L container at constant temperature: H2(g) + I2(g) ⇌ 2 HI(g). Each molecule drawn represents 0.010 mol.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: (i) Identify evidence from the diagrams that the system is at equilibrium. (ii) A student says that because nothing changes between t1 and t2, the reactions have stopped. Explain why the student is incorrect.

rubric.point: (i) The numbers of each kind of molecule are the same at t₁ and t₂.
accept: constant composition: 2 H₂, 2 I₂, 6 HI in both

rubric.point: (ii) Equilibrium is dynamic: H₂ and I₂ keep forming HI and HI keeps decomposing, at equal rates, so the counts stay constant.
accept: forward rate = reverse rate, both nonzero

parts.sample: (i) Both snapshots contain 2 H<sub>2</sub>, 2 I<sub>2</sub> and 6 HI, so the composition is not changing. (ii) The forward and reverse reactions are still occurring; they happen at equal rates, so each molecule that forms is matched by one that reacts, and the counts stay the same.

rubric.point: Converts counts to concentrations: [H₂] = [I₂] = 0.020 M, [HI] = 0.060 M.
accept: states that counts may be used because the gas moles are equal on both sides

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: At constant temperature, the volume of the container is suddenly reduced to 0.50 L. (i) Determine whether the amount of HI changes as the system responds. Justify your answer by comparing Q with K. (ii) Draw a particle diagram of the 0.50 L container once equilibrium is re-established, using the same key.

rubric.point: (i) Claim: the amount of HI does not change (no shift).
(ii-justification) Halving the volume doubles every concentration; Q = (2[HI])² / ((2[H₂])(2[I₂])) = Q₀ = K, so Q still equals K.
accept: the factors of 4 cancel because the gas moles are equal on both sides, so Q = K

rubric.point: Drawing: a smaller box with 2 H₂, 2 I₂ and 6 HI, atoms conserved.
accept: same counts as before in a box about half the size

parts.sample: (i) The amount of HI does not change. Halving the volume doubles every concentration, so Q = (2 × 0.060)<sup>2</sup> / ((2 × 0.020)(2 × 0.020)) = 0.0144 / 0.0016 = 9.0, which still equals K. With Q = K there is no net reaction. (ii) The drawing shows a container half the size holding 2 H<sub>2</sub>, 2 I<sub>2</sub> and 6 HI molecules.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Starting again from the original 1.0 L equilibrium mixture, 4 more H2 molecules (0.040 mol) are injected at constant temperature. (i) Calculate Q immediately after the injection. (ii) Justify the direction of the net reaction that follows.

rubric.point: (ii) Q = 3.0 < K = 9.0, so the net reaction proceeds forward (toward HI) until Q = K.
accept: Q < K, net forward; no credit for "K increases" or rate language alone

parts.sample: (i) [H<sub>2</sub>] = 6 × 0.010 mol / 1.0 L = 0.060 M. Q = (0.060)<sup>2</sup> / ((0.060)(0.020)) = 3.0. (ii) Q = 3.0 is less than K = 9.0, so the net reaction proceeds forward, consuming H<sub>2</sub> and I<sub>2</sub> and forming HI, until Q equals K.

parts.label: e
parts.prompt: Explain why, after the system in part (d) returns to equilibrium, the value of Kc is still 9.0.

rubric.point: K depends only on temperature, which did not change; adding H₂ changed Q, and the system shifted until Q equaled the same K.
accept: temperature is constant, so K is constant

parts.sample: The temperature did not change, and K depends only on temperature. Adding H<sub>2</sub> changed Q, not K; the net forward reaction continued until Q was again equal to 9.0.
